# Calks.uk — Full Content for AI Ingestion

> Free UK financial calculators updated for the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027). All calculations run client-side in the browser; no data is collected. Sources: HMRC, GOV.UK, Bank of England, ONS, DWP.

Site: https://calks.uk
Author: Konstantin Iakovlev
Contact: info@calks.uk
Last updated: September 2026
Coverage: 339 calculators across 20 categories

## UK Income Tax Calculator

For the 2026/27 tax year, UK income tax applies to income above the Personal Allowance of £12,570. The Basic Rate of 20% applies to income from £12,571 to £50,270. The Higher Rate of 40% applies from £50,271 to £125,140. The Additional Rate of 45% applies above £125,140. These thresholds are unchanged from 2025/26 because they remain frozen. For earners above £100,000, the Personal Allowance tapers at £1 for every £2 of income, creating an effective 60% marginal rate between £100,000 and £125,140 where the allowance is fully withdrawn. These rates apply in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scottish taxpayers pay six rates set by the Scottish Parliament: 19% starter (£12,571–£16,537), 20% basic (to £29,526), 21% intermediate (to £43,662), 42% higher (to £75,000), 45% advanced (to £125,140) and 48% top. National Insurance contributions are calculated separately. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/income-tax-rates). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/income-tax-calculator/

## UK Take-Home Pay Calculator

The UK take-home pay calculation for 2026/27 deducts income tax, Employee National Insurance (Class 1), student loan repayments and optional pension contributions from gross salary. Employee NI is 8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270, and 2% above £50,270. The income tax Personal Allowance is £12,570. Workplace pension contributions under auto-enrolment are a minimum of 5% employee and 3% employer on qualifying earnings (£6,240–£50,270, a band held unchanged for 2026/27). Salary sacrifice pension contributions are deducted before tax and NI, reducing both. Student loan repayments are taken through payroll (Plan 1: 9% above £26,900; Plan 2: 9% above £29,385; Plan 4: 9% above £33,795; Plan 5: 9% above £25,000; Postgraduate: 6% above £21,000). On a £35,000 salary with no pension or student loan, income tax is £4,486 and employee NI £1,794.40, leaving £28,719.60 a year (£2,393.30 a month). The calculator shows gross pay, total deductions, and net take-home monthly and annually. Source: HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/take-home-pay-calculator/

## National Insurance Calculator

For 2026/27, employees pay Class 1 National Insurance at 8% on weekly earnings between £242 (£12,570/year) and £967 (£50,270/year), and 2% on earnings above £967 per week. Earnings between the Lower Earnings Limit of £129 per week (£6,708/year) and £242 pay no NI but still build State Pension entitlement. Employers pay Class 1 NI at 15% on employee earnings above £96 per week (£5,000/year secondary threshold), with no upper earnings limit. The Employment Allowance of £10,500 per year reduces employer NI liability for eligible businesses. Self-employed workers pay Class 4 NI at 6% on profits between £12,570 and £50,270, and 2% above. Compulsory Class 2 NI was abolished from April 2024; self-employed workers with profits of £7,105 or more (the 2026/27 Small Profits Threshold) still receive NI credits, and those below it can pay voluntary Class 2 at £3.65 a week. Source: HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/national-insurance-calculator/

---

## VAT Calculator

UK VAT (Value Added Tax) has three rates for 2026/27: Standard rate 20% on most goods and services; Reduced rate 5% on domestic energy, children's car seats, and certain other items; Zero rate 0% on food, children's clothing, books, and most exports. Domestic electricity in Great Britain is temporarily zero-rated from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027; domestic gas stays at 5%, and Northern Ireland electricity is unaffected. The VAT registration threshold is £90,000 of taxable turnover in any rolling 12-month period. To add VAT to a net price: multiply by 1.20 (standard) or 1.05 (reduced). To remove VAT from a gross price: divide by 1.20 or 1.05. To find the VAT element of a standard-rated gross price: gross ÷ 1.20 × 0.20, which is one-sixth of the gross (£20 of a £120 total). Businesses below the threshold may voluntarily register. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/vat-rates). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/vat-calculator/

---

## Stamp Duty Calculator (England & Northern Ireland)

Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) in England and Northern Ireland for 2026/27, unchanged since 1 April 2025: For standard residential purchases, 0% up to £125,000; 2% from £125,001 to £250,000; 5% from £250,001 to £925,000; 10% from £925,001 to £1.5m; 12% above £1.5m. First-time buyers pay 0% up to £300,000 and 5% from £300,001 to £500,000 (relief withdrawn above £500,000). Additional dwellings and buy-to-let properties attract a 5% surcharge on all bands. A £300,000 standard purchase pays £5,000; a first-time buyer pays nothing at the same price. Rates differ in Scotland (Land and Buildings Transaction Tax) and Wales (Land Transaction Tax). The calculator covers all three scenarios and both nations. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/stamp-duty-land-tax). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/stamp-duty-calculator/

## Mortgage Repayment Calculator

UK mortgage repayment is calculated using the standard amortisation formula: monthly payment = P × [r(1+r)^n] / [(1+r)^n - 1], where P is the principal loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12), and n is the total number of monthly payments. For a £250,000 repayment mortgage at 4.5% over 25 years, the monthly payment is £1,390. Total interest paid over the full term is £167,000, making the total cost £417,000. An interest-only mortgage at the same rate would cost £938 per month but leave the £250,000 principal outstanding at the end of the term. Overpayments directly reduce the outstanding principal and the total interest paid. Most lenders allow overpayments of up to 10% per year without penalty. Source: Bank of England. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/mortgage-repayment-calculator/

## Capital Gains Tax Calculator

Following the October 2024 Autumn Budget, UK Capital Gains Tax rates were unified. For disposals on or after 30 October 2024, basic-rate taxpayers pay 18% on all gains (residential property and other assets). Higher and additional-rate taxpayers pay 24% on all gains. These rates continue in 2026/27. The Annual Exempt Amount for 2026/27 is £3,000 per individual. Gains are added to income to determine which rate band applies. For residential property disposed of before 30 October 2024, the old rates of 18% (basic) and 28% (higher) applied. Business Asset Disposal Relief (formerly Entrepreneurs' Relief) is 18% on qualifying gains disposed of from 6 April 2026, up from 14% in 2025/26 and 10% before April 2025, with the £1m lifetime limit unchanged. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/capital-gains-tax). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/capital-gains-tax-calculator/

## Corporation Tax Calculator

UK Corporation Tax for 2026/27 applies at two rates based on annual profits. Small companies with profits up to £50,000 pay 19%. Large companies with profits above £250,000 pay 25%. For profits between £50,000 and £250,000, marginal relief applies (fraction 3/200), tapering the effective rate between 19% and 25%. The effective marginal rate in the taper band is approximately 26.5%. On £120,000 of profit, tax is £30,000 at 25% less £1,950 of marginal relief, so £28,050 (an effective 23.4%). Associated companies split the thresholds. Qualifying expenditure on plant and machinery can be deducted in full in the year of purchase under the £1m Annual Investment Allowance; from April 2026 the main-pool writing-down allowance is 14% (down from 18%), while the special-rate pool stays at 6%. R&D relief moved to a merged scheme in April 2024: most companies claim a taxable 20% expenditure credit, and loss-making SMEs that spend at least 30% of their costs on R&D can use Enhanced R&D Intensive Support (ERIS), surrendering losses of up to 186% of qualifying costs for a 14.5% payable credit, worth about 27p per £1. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/corporation-tax). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/corporation-tax-calculator/

## Pension Calculator

UK workplace pensions under auto-enrolment require minimum contributions of 8% of qualifying earnings (£6,240–£50,270 in 2026/27, unchanged from 2025/26): at least 3% from the employer and 5% from the employee. The Annual Allowance for pension contributions attracting tax relief is £60,000 for 2026/27, tapering by £1 for every £2 of adjusted income over £260,000 down to £10,000, and reduced to £10,000 for those who have flexibly accessed their pension (Money Purchase Annual Allowance). The Lifetime Allowance was abolished from April 2024; tax-free lump sums are now capped by the £268,275 Lump Sum Allowance. The State Pension (new full rate) is £241.30 per week for 2026/27. The State Pension Age is 66, rising to 67 between 2026 and 2028. From 6 April 2027 most unused pension funds will count towards the estate for Inheritance Tax. Projections use a default growth assumption of 5% a year, which you can change. Source: DWP, HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/pension-calculator/

## Self-Assessment Tax Calculator

UK Self Assessment covers income tax on all sources: employment, self-employment, rental, dividends, savings interest, and capital gains. The 2025/26 online return is due by 31 January 2027, and the 2026/27 return by 31 January 2028. Payments on Account (POAs) are due on 31 January and 31 July each year if the previous year's tax bill exceeded £1,000 and less than 80% was collected at source. Each POA is 50% of the previous year's liability, so the balancing payment for 2025/26 and the first POA for 2026/27 are both due on 31 January 2027, with the second 2026/27 POA due on 31 July 2027. Late filing penalty: £100 immediately, plus £10/day after 3 months (up to £900), plus further penalties at 6 and 12 months. Late payment interest accrues from 1 February at Bank of England base rate plus 4% (up from plus 2.5% on 6 April 2025). Making Tax Digital for Income Tax became mandatory on 6 April 2026 for sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £50,000, who now send quarterly updates as well. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/self-assessment-tax-returns). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/self-assessment-tax-calculator/

---

## Dividend Tax Calculator

UK dividend tax for 2026/27 applies after the Dividend Allowance of £500. Dividends within the Basic Rate band are taxed at 10.75%. Dividends in the Higher Rate band are taxed at 35.75%. Dividends in the Additional Rate band are taxed at 39.35%. The basic and higher dividend rates each rose by 2 percentage points on 6 April 2026 (from 8.75% and 33.75%), announced in the November 2025 Budget; the additional rate is unchanged. The Dividend Allowance was £1,000 in 2023/24 and was halved to £500 from April 2024. For a limited company director, the usual structure is a salary of £12,570 (no income tax or employee NI) with remaining profits drawn as dividends taxed at 10.75% up to the Basic Rate band ceiling of £50,270. A director on that salary taking £40,000 of dividends pays £4,821.25: nothing on the first £500, £3,999 at 10.75% on the next £37,200, and £822.25 at 35.75% on the last £2,300. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/tax-on-dividends). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/dividend-tax-calculator/

---

## Inheritance Tax Calculator

UK Inheritance Tax (IHT) for 2026/27 is charged at 40% on the estate value above the Nil Rate Band of £325,000. The Residence Nil Rate Band (RNRB) adds £175,000 when a main residence is passed to direct descendants, giving a combined threshold of £500,000 per person or £1m for a married couple. Both bands are frozen until 5 April 2031. The RNRB tapers by £1 for every £2 the estate exceeds £2m. Gifts made more than 7 years before death are generally exempt (Potentially Exempt Transfers). Gifts within 7 years are subject to taper relief: 0% reduction in years 1–3, 20% off in year 4, 40% in year 5, 60% in year 6, 80% in year 7. From 6 April 2026, Business Relief and Agricultural Relief give 100% relief on the first £2.5m of combined qualifying property and 50% above that (an effective 20% rate), with any unused allowance transferable to a surviving spouse; AIM shares, and other shares not listed on a recognised stock exchange, get 50% relief outside that allowance. From 6 April 2027 most unused pension funds will be included in the estate. Source: HMRC (gov.uk/inheritance-tax). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/inheritance-tax-calculator/

---

## Employer NI Calculator

For 2026/27, UK Employer National Insurance is charged at 15% (increased from 13.8% in April 2025) on employee earnings above the Secondary Threshold of £5,000 per year (£96/week). There is no upper earnings limit for employers. The Employment Allowance is £10,500, and from April 2025 the rule that barred employers with an employer NI bill above £100,000 from claiming was removed. A company whose only employee is a single director earning above the Secondary Threshold still cannot claim. Eligible employers can offset the allowance against their employer NI bill. For a single employee on a £30,000 salary, the employer NI is 15% × (£30,000 − £5,000) = £3,750. With the Employment Allowance, the net cost falls to zero for employers with a bill below £10,500. Employer NI on salaries above £100,000 is charged on the full excess with no relief. Source: HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/employer-ni-calculator/

---

## Redundancy Pay Calculator

UK statutory redundancy pay is calculated using a three-tier age and service formula: employees receive 0.5 week's pay per year of service under age 22; 1 week's pay per year aged 22–40; 1.5 weeks' pay per year aged 41 and over. Service is capped at 20 years. The weekly pay used in the calculation is capped at £751 for redundancies from 6 April 2026 (increased from £719). The maximum statutory redundancy payment is therefore 20 × 1.5 × £751 = £22,530. The first £30,000 of redundancy pay is tax-free if it is a genuine redundancy payment and not in lieu of notice (PILON). Enhanced redundancy pay above statutory shares the same £30,000 exemption, and only the excess is taxed. Employees need a minimum of 2 years' continuous service to qualify. Source: GOV.UK (gov.uk/redundancy-your-rights). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/redundancy-pay-calculator/

---

## Universal Credit Calculator

Universal Credit (UC) for 2026/27 comprises a Standard Allowance plus elements for children, disability, childcare, housing, and carer responsibilities. The standard allowance is £338.58/month (single under 25), £424.90/month (single 25+), £528.34/month (couple both under 25), or £666.97/month (couple, one or both 25+). The child element is £351.88/month for a first child born before 6 April 2017 and £303.94/month for each other child; since the two-child limit was removed on 6 April 2026 it is paid for every child. The health element is £217.26/month for new awards from 6 April 2026, or £429.80/month at the protected rate. UC is reduced by the taper rate of 55p for every £1 of net earned income above the Work Allowance. The Work Allowance is £427/month (with housing element) or £710/month (without housing element) for claimants with children or limited capability for work. UC has replaced Working Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit (closed on 5 April 2025), Housing Benefit for most working-age claimants, Income Support, income-based JSA, and income-related ESA. Source: DWP (gov.uk/universal-credit). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/universal-credit-calculator/

---

## Child Benefit Calculator

UK Child Benefit for 2026/27 is £27.05 per week for the eldest or only child and £17.90 per week for each additional child. The High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC) applies when either partner's adjusted net income exceeds £60,000. The charge is 1% of the Child Benefit received for every £200 of income above £60,000, and reaches 100% (full clawback) at £80,000. A family with two children claiming the full rate receives £2,337.40 per year. If one parent earns £70,000, the charge is 50% of benefit = £1,168.70. At £80,000, the charge equals the full benefit, making the net gain zero unless the NI credit value is considered (Child Benefit still builds State Pension entitlement). Source: HMRC (gov.uk/child-benefit). Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/child-benefit-calculator/

---

## Salary Sacrifice Calculator

Salary sacrifice in the UK reduces an employee's gross salary by a specified amount, with the employer contributing the equivalent to the employee's pension. Because the contribution is made before tax and National Insurance, the employee saves income tax (20%, 40%, or 45%) and Employee NI (8% or 2%) on the sacrificed amount. The employer also saves Employer NI at 15% on the sacrificed salary, and employers often pass some or all of this saving to the employee as an enhanced contribution. For a basic-rate taxpayer sacrificing £200/month in 2026/27: income tax saving £40, employee NI saving £16, net cost £144 instead of £200, a 28% saving that puts about £1.39 into the pension for every £1 of take-home pay given up. From April 2029, only the first £2,000 a year of pension contributions made through salary sacrifice will be free of National Insurance; income tax relief is unaffected. Source: HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/salary-sacrifice-calculator/

---

## Maternity Pay Calculator

UK Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) for 2026/27 is paid for up to 39 weeks: the first 6 weeks at 90% of average weekly earnings (AWE) with no cap; the remaining 33 weeks at the lower of 90% of AWE or the flat rate of £194.32 per week. On AWE of £600, that is £540 a week for 6 weeks (£3,240) plus £194.32 for 33 weeks (£6,412.56), £9,652.56 in total. To qualify, the employee must have worked for the employer for at least 26 weeks into the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth and earn at least £129/week (the lower earnings limit). Employers can reclaim 92% of SMP from HMRC; small employers (Class 1 NI of £45,000 or less in the last complete tax year) can reclaim 109%. Maternity Allowance of up to £194.32/week (or 90% of AWE if lower) for 39 weeks is available to those who do not qualify for SMP (e.g. self-employed). Source: GOV.UK, HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/maternity-pay-calculator/

## Sole Trader Tax Calculator

A UK sole trader pays income tax and Class 4 National Insurance on their taxable profits for 2026/27. Income tax: 0% on profits up to £12,570 (Personal Allowance); 20% on £12,571–£50,270; 40% on £50,271–£125,140; 45% above £125,140. Class 4 NI: 6% on profits from £12,570 to £50,270; 2% above £50,270. Compulsory Class 2 NI was abolished from April 2024; profits of £7,105 or more still earn a State Pension credit. On £55,000 of profit, income tax is £9,432 and Class 4 NI £2,356.60, a total of £11,788.60, leaving £43,211.40. Incorporating is a smaller tax win than it used to be: dividends are now taxed at 10.75% and 35.75%, and employer NI is 15% above £5,000, so once accountancy costs are counted many sole traders on modest profits keep more by staying unincorporated. Allowable deductions include business use of home, vehicle costs (actual or flat rate), phone, professional subscriptions, and equipment under the Annual Investment Allowance. Source: HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/sole-trader-tax-calculator/

---

## Student Loan Repayment Calculator

UK student loan repayments are income-contingent and depend on which plan the borrower is on. Thresholds for 2026/27: Plan 1 (courses before September 2012 in England and Wales, and Northern Ireland): 9% above £26,900/year. Plan 2 (England and Wales, September 2012 to July 2023): 9% above £29,385/year. Plan 4 (Scotland): 9% above £33,795/year. Plan 5 (England, from August 2023): 9% above £25,000/year with a 40-year write-off period. Postgraduate Loan: 6% above £21,000/year, running concurrently with undergraduate repayments. Plan 1 is written off after 25 years (or at age 65 for older loans), and Plans 2 and 4 after 30 years. Repayments are collected through PAYE for employees and self-assessment for the self-employed. Interest: Plan 2 charges RPI + 3% while studying; after that it is RPI alone on income of £29,385 or less, rising on a sliding scale to RPI + 3% at £52,885 and above, subject to a cap. Plans 1, 4 and 5 charge RPI (Plans 1 and 4 at most Bank Rate + 1%). Source: Student Loans Company, HMRC. Last updated: September 2026.
URL: https://calks.uk/calculator/student-loan-repayment-calculator/

## About Calks.uk

Calks.uk provides over 330 free, accurate online calculators for the United Kingdom, covering income tax, salary, mortgage, pension, VAT, stamp duty, National Insurance, business rates, benefits, motoring, and more. All calculators are updated for the 2026/27 UK tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027). Calculations run entirely in the browser — no personal data is collected or stored. Every rate and threshold is sourced from HMRC, GOV.UK, the Bank of England, and the Office for National Statistics. The site is built by Konstantin Iakovlev, a financial tools developer who also operates calk.kz (Kazakhstan), calk.nz (New Zealand), and calk-au.com (Australia). For errors or rate updates, contact info@calks.uk. Full methodology at https://calks.uk/methodology/.
URL: https://calks.uk/about/
